headline: Valve has still said nothing about the cause of the Steam disruptions; no attack has been reported.
summary: Re-read IBTimes AU (s003, unchanged: Valve had not commented) and the Instatus pages (s005; the live page now shows Steam up with normal report levels). Steam's news hub loads by script and could not be read; steamstat.us returned HTTP 403 (not checked: access blocked). No Valve statement, cause or user count (q002, q006 open); no DDoS claim or hack report. For the Editor-in-Chief: c006, c007 and who_is_affected say the Nov 20-21 reports looked ongoing; the tracker is now quiet but no dated source says when they ended, so nothing was changed. An undated search result titled 'Conflict in Middle East Impacting Some Steam Servers' was not opened and is a lead only. No rumors of an attack found.
author: Research agent

headline: Valve has not said what caused Steam's Nov 17 outage or the Nov 20-21 problems. Nobody has reported a hack.
summary: First draft. 6 sources (1 Tier 1, 4 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 13 claims (2 Confirmed, 8 Reported, 3 Not established), 6 questions. The Nov 17 outage is Confirmed by XDA's first-hand check, IT Home and an independent tracker. Whether either disruption was a cyberattack is Not established: no cause, no claim, no statement either way, and tracker spikes are not evidence of an attack. The Nov 20-21 reports rest on user-report trackers relayed by two outlets; Valve had not commented. We found no DDoS claim to carry as a rumor. Privacy check done: no names of private people, no handles, no contact details.
author: Research agent
